top.title: XXRI-OS explores the lowest end of the Linux desktop
top.description: New Linux distros seem to appear daily, but far too few distinguish themselves by being smaller and simpler. XXRI OS is a fairly new desktop Linux distro. It has a snazzy-looking website, complete with an amusing URL, and along similar lines, its GitHub page has a very heavily formatted README. Nonetheless, this is not another over-complex opinionated slopfest of an OS with built-in AI, bizarre keystrokes, and several proprietary components. It's almost the reverse. The main download is just 287.4 MB, and that's the full distro, not a minimalist installer that fetches most of the OS over your internet connection. We installed it in a VirtualBox VM. It took 675 MB of disk space, and in the graphical desktop, when we opened a terminal window, it reported just 75 MB of RAM in use with the desktop and terminal running. We are restraining ourselves hard when we say that those are unusually low numbers for the 2020s. We would expect most cut-down lightweight Linux distros to use around five to 10 times as much disk space or memory. The current release of XXRI-OS is version 2.7. XXRI OS 1.0 came out in May 2025, making this a young project with five published releases already behind it. It also has much deeper roots: it is based on the existing and much older Tiny Core Linux . The Reg FOSS desk last looked at Tiny Core Linux 15 back in March 2024 and the project is still going strong: the latest version is version 17.1. Tiny Core Linux is a marvel, but there are prices to pay for somehow getting a graphical Linux desktop into a 23 MB download. It runs from RAM and uses its own extension-based package system, which can make adding components and managing updates unfamiliar territory. XXRI OS takes TCL and turns it into a slightly more conventional desktop. It installs to disk in the usual way, and it includes the core functions that most people would expect from their OS in 2026. It has a file manager, a text editor, a media player, a simple app store for adding further components, and a settings app including an update manager. It even includes its own web browser, and there are both x86-32 and x86-64 variants. The desktop layout has a floating dock at bottom center, and the icons are unlabelled. To save you some guesswork, though, floating just to the left of the dock is an icon with a grid of dots, which is an app launcher. The icons in that do have text labels underneath, so you can learn which symbol denotes which function from here. We plan to experiment more with this remarkable little OS and see how well it runs on the oldest, slowest boxes in the Irish Sea wing of Vulture Towers, but we like what we see so far. It's an impressive experiment in how low Linux can go and remain useful. While Tiny Core Linux goes down to Windows 95 levels of resource usage, XXRI OS has a more usable Windows 2000-level baseline. Over a quarter of a century later, that is nearly unbeatable. ®

nigeria.title: Trump, Putin, Xi agree to nuclear risk talks
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have agreed to hold talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China. The agreement was contained in a joint declaration issued by the White House on Thursday after the meeting, during which the three leaders discussed the international situation and pledged to promote strategic stability and international security. The United States, Russia and China, which are permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, also committed to reforming the UN to enable it to respond more effectively to global challenges and strengthen its role in maintaining international peace and security. The three countries further indicated plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, while reaffirming the importance of stable energy flows. The leaders also addressed issues relating to the immunity of state officials and the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court (ICC), warning against what they described as the abuse of jurisdiction by the court and similar bodies. Trump and Putin also expressed appreciation to China for hosting the trilateral summit. The joint declaration read in part: “The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. “As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, the United States, Russia, and China committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. “The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. “The three heads of state recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of state officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.” The post Trump, Putin, Xi agree to nuclear risk talks appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, Akande says
nigeria.description: A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has urged President Bola Tinubu to grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, saying the local media should have the opportunity to hold the President accountable. Akande made the call on Thursday while reacting to the controversy surrounding Tinubu’s interview with American political strategist and lobbyist, Diana London. He said he had no objection to the President granting an interview to a foreign journalist but questioned why Nigerian journalists had not been given similar opportunities to ask him questions on issues of national importance. “I wish the President were also having interviews with Nigerian journalists. That’s my own main issue with this development. “It’s not a bad thing that the President has chosen to have this interview; my worry is that he’s leaving out the Nigerian press. Why has he not made himself available for Nigerians to interrogate him?” he said. On allegations that London received $4.5 million in connection with the engagement, Akande said the strategist had denied being paid as a lobbyist by the Federal Government for the interview. He, however, called for greater transparency from the government to clarify the circumstances surrounding the engagement. “As to the controversy whether this woman (Diana) was paid, the woman has denied that she was doing this as a paid lobbyist of the Federal Government. The ADC people are saying that there should be more clarity, there should be more transparency, yes. “Let the Federal Government also give us more facts that this is not a paid-for interview. The most important thing is that Nigerians should be given the opportunity to interview Mr President,” Akande said. The former presidential spokesman also recalled his experience in the Presidential Villa during the administration of ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, when Osinbajo served as Vice-President. He said he considered it inappropriate for journalists invited to interview the President or Vice-President to demand payment for the opportunity. “My own experience in the Villa, I wasn’t aware of any payment for an interview and I expressed this. When we were in the Villa, I considered it an insult to have an opportunity to interview the President and the Vice-President and be asking for money. The President of a country is the numero uno,” he said. The controversy followed reports alleging that London received $4.5 million in connection with a lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government. nigeria.description: The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from parading himself as the Senior Pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin according to TheCable, granted the order on Wednesday following a suit instituted by the incorporated trustees of the church. The trustees had sought a pre-emptive order of injunction restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and interfering with its activities, governance and other affairs. They argued that Odukoya had ceased to hold the position following the appointment of a successor by the late founder and Senior Pastor of the church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. In the suit, the trustees sought an order restraining Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting, meddling with or obstructing the activities and governance of the church pending compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on pre-action protocol. Granting the application, Justice Adewunmi-Oshin ruled: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to commence this action under the Pre-Action Protocol pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.” The order followed the trustees’ application for judicial intervention in the leadership and administration of the church. nigeria.title: 2027: Atiku demands scrutiny of INEC’s AI system for processing election results
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to open its proposed artificial intelligence system for processing election results to independent audit ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku wants the commission to disclose how the technology works, who developed it and what safeguards are in place to prevent valid polling unit results from being flagged, delayed or excluded during electronic processing. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said he had petitioned the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and allied democratic stakeholders, demanding algorithmic transparency, independent scrutiny and clear rules for human oversight. The petition follows INEC’s announced integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System, DIVAS, with the INEC Result Viewing portal, IReV. Warning against placing public confidence in an opaque technology, Atiku said: “INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward.” He demanded publication of the system’s technical and operational framework, including its training data sources, criteria for flagging discrepancies and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors. He also wants independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists to have access to the source code, training data and decision logs for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026. On the legal status of polling unit results, Atiku insisted that the physical Form EC8A, completed and signed at the polling unit, must remain the primary evidence of what transpired there, warning against allowing an algorithmic assessment to override it. “The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment. “A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he said. Atiku also demanded a transparent procedure for reviewing flagged result sheets, including the officials responsible for such reviews, documentation of decisions, notification of political parties and mechanisms for promptly challenging errors. nigeria.title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election, Soludo says
nigeria.description: Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest. Soludo made the declaration on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, where he argued that the APC had a stronger nationwide political presence than its opponents. “This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said. Explaining his position, the governor said the APC presidential ticket was facing opposition candidates whose political influence, according to him, was limited to certain parts of the country. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said. He also attributed his confidence to the performance of the Tinubu administration, arguing that the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima deserved another term based on their record in office. “President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said. The governor further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election. “And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. “And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said. Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, claiming that there was a consensus among people familiar with the economy, both locally and internationally, that the administration was moving in the right direction. He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, as one of the initiatives through which the administration was addressing the needs of Nigerians. nigeria.title: Kwara South: APC candidate Adewoye confident of victory
nigeria.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has expressed confidence in his ability to represent the people of the district effectively, saying his business experience and grassroots interventions have prepared him for public service. Adewoye said his conviction was anchored on more than three decades of experience in business, philanthropic activities and commitment to grassroots development. Speaking in an interview with journalists, the industrialist said he was passionate about translating his private-sector experience into public service, despite not having previously held an elective position or served as a political appointee. Addressing concerns about his lack of political experience and the challenge posed by established opposition politicians, Adewoye said he was confident of earning the support of voters. “I am convinced of my capacity and believe I have what it takes to represent the people effectively,” he said. He argued that voters should assess candidates based on their records, capacity and acceptability rather than previous political positions alone. nigeria.title: Man accused of AI-assisted exam cheating found dead in Seoul
nigeria.description: A South Korean man suspected of using artificial intelligence (AI) to obtain a perfect score in the country’s law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul. Lee Jin-woo was discovered at a motel in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong District, eastern Seoul, at about 1:12 p.m. on Thursday, emergency authorities said. According to Yonhap News TV, a note was also found at the scene, reportedly indicating that Lee was physically and mentally exhausted. However, the note reportedly contained no admission of cheating or explanation of the allegations against him. Authorities said they would examine the scene to establish the circumstances surrounding his death. Lee had attracted public attention over allegations that he used AI to cheat in the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), the examination required for admission into law schools in South Korea. In an attempt to dispel the suspicions, he had announced plans to answer questions from the Korean language section of the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test in real time on Thursday morning. However, he failed to appear at the designated venue by 8:40 a.m., when the examination began. Police launched a search after receiving a report at about 8:42 a.m. expressing concern over his whereabouts. According to the police, Lee left his home on Wednesday and travelled to a lodging facility in Gwangjin District, eastern Seoul, before leaving on Thursday morning. He reportedly took a taxi towards Songpa District, southern Seoul, between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., before heading to Gangdong District, where his body was later discovered. Lee had previously gained attention after revealing that he had scored between the sixth and eighth tiers in previous college entrance examinations, which use a nine-tier grading system, with higher numbers representing lower scores. He said he later developed a better understanding of studying and reading comprehension, eventually gaining admission into Korea University’s Department of Political Science and International Relations in 2024 and Seoul National University’s School of Dentistry in 2026. He also reportedly achieved a perfect score in the LEET while attending Seoul National University. However, his academic achievements came under scrutiny following allegations of AI-assisted cheating in a national tax accountant certification examination. Questions were subsequently raised over whether he had also used AI to cheat in the LEET and the college entrance examinations for the 2024 and 2026 academic years. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on Wednesday that it had assigned a criminal complaint against Lee, bordering on allegations of obstruction of business, obstruction of official duties and fraud, to its Provincial Special Detective Corps. Following his death, police are expected to close the case without prosecution, as criminal proceedings cannot continue against a deceased suspect. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life Church postpones 2026 Thanksgiving service
nigeria.description: The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, amid an ongoing leadership crisis involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees. The Lagos-based church announced the postponement in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19. The notice read, “Please be informed that our Thanksgiving 2026 Service, previously scheduled for Sunday, November 22, has been postponed. A new date will be communicated in due course.” The church did not give any reason for the decision or indicate when the service would be rescheduled. The development comes amid a leadership dispute following an announcement by some members of the Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as the church’s senior pastor with immediate effect. The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and a December 2021 video recording in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined succession arrangements that identified another individual as his preferred successor, while assigning Jimmy Odukoya administrative and youth church responsibilities. They also cited governance concerns and issues surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage. However, Odukoya and representatives of the church rejected the announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and not a decision properly taken by the Board of Trustees. They maintained that he remains the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the board, following his unanimous approval for the positions in September 2023 after his father’s death. The trustees subsequently reaffirmed their position and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to provide interim spiritual and administrative leadership pending further consultations. The crisis has also extended to the control of the church’s official social media accounts, with both sides reportedly disputing authority over the platforms. Odukoya was notably absent from the church’s midweek service on Thursday as the leadership dispute continued. The Thanksgiving service had attracted attention amid the unfolding crisis, with the postponement adding another development to the dispute over the church’s leadership and administration. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Global Securities Watchdog Warns of Quantum Computing Threat to Blockchains and Finance The International Organization of Securities Commissions, the global body for securities regulators, published a 63-page report on Thursday warning that quantum computing is a “significant medium to long-term cybersecurity challenge” for financial markets, and that moving blockchains to quantum-resistant cryptography may be especially hard. IOSCO said no practical quantum computer capable of compromising widely used cryptography exists today. “The scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today,” said Jean-Paul Servais, chair of the IOSCO board, in the release. The final report drew on a survey of IOSCO members and interviews with industry experts and market participants. The group found that preparedness across the financial sector remains at an early stage. Most firms are still raising awareness, setting up governance and taking inventory of the cryptography they use, while migration testing and rollout are limited. Firms cited reliance on third parties, interoperability, limited expertise and unclear timelines as common obstacles. Why blockchains face a harder quantum migration IOSCO said the problem is sharper for public blockchains because cryptography is built into their core design. Replacing it requires hard forks and coordinated action across thousands of independent validators and node operators, and decentralized networks have no way to force a fast upgrade. The report said that could make any migration “slow and fragmented.” The report also flagged the cost of the new cryptography. It said signatures from ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, run about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than the 64-byte signatures common today. That could strain throughput, storage and fees. IOSCO cited testing on Solana’s quantum-resistant testnet that showed throughput falling by about 90%. On exposed coins, the report said a capable attacker could derive private keys from public keys that are already visible on a network, and that uneven migration could leave those assets vulnerable. It singled out dormant or abandoned assets tied to exposed keys, which may be hard to move if the holders cannot be identified or cannot act. IOSCO did not mention bitcoin by name. The report’s blockchain examples were Ethereum, Solana and Tron. How soon could the threat arrive? Timing remains uncertain. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Ledger Finds Tampered Hardware Wallets in Berlin, Probes Two in Dubai Ledger has confirmed tampered hardware wallets in Berlin and is investigating two more in Dubai, the wallet maker said Wednesday, widening a probe into spy implants it first traced to resellers in Southeast Asia in October. The new cases are “the same incident,” Ledger said in an update on its support site. Every device it has confirmed carries the same physical modification, built to capture a user’s recovery phrase while the wallet is being set up. “There is no flaw in Ledger’s secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com,” the company wrote on X. Ledger also found one affected Nano Gen5, its newer model, among the Southeast Asian resellers it had already paused. It did not give a count for Berlin, describing the cases there only as “a few tampered units.” Berlin buyers told to check in Ledger asked anyone who bought one of its devices in Berlin since January 2026 to contact its support team. In Dubai, the company said it is working with distribution partners to learn how the two suspected units entered circulation. Its Donjon security team is examining suspected devices, and resellers have been asked to pause sales wherever inspections are still running. Customers who are worried about a device should stop using it and should not open it themselves, Ledger said. Its advice is to move funds to a new wallet created on a device bought directly from ledger.com, without reusing the old recovery phrase or passphrase, because a tampered unit can capture both. The company also told affected users to file a report with local authorities. For a limited time, Ledger is offering physical inspections, including X-rays, at its factory in Vierzon, France. “This continues to be a small number of devices overall, and we do expect more to be discovered in our investigation and via social media,” Ledger said. How the implant works The probe began in October, after users in Southeast Asia reported drained wallets. Ledger linked the cases to devices sold through CryptoBilis, a Malaysia-based authorized reseller, and asked it to stop selling and shipping Ledger products, BleepingComputer reported . entertainment.title: From Tunde Kelani to Akinola Davies Jr., 5 Nollywood Directors You Should Know
entertainment.description: From music visuals to international festival stages and actor-turned-director debuts, Dammy Twitch, Akinola Davies Jr., and Daniel Etim Effiong represent different paths into Nollywood directing. Think about the Nigerian films and series you have watched recently, the ones that kept you glued to your screen, had you talking about the storyline long after the credits rolled or recommending them to everyone you know. While the actors are often the faces you remember first, there is someone behind the camera whose creative choices help bring those stories to life: the director. From interpreting the script and guiding actors to shaping how each scene looks, sounds and unfolds, directors influence almost every part of what ends up on screen. As Nollywood grows in ambition, production quality and global reach, the filmmakers steering these projects are becoming just as central to the industry’s story as the stars in front of the lens. Some have spent decades bringing Nigerian literature and history to the screen, while others are earning international acclaim or crossing over from music videos into feature films. Here are five Nollywood directors whose work is worth knowing. Tunde Kelani Start with Tunde Kelani if you want to see where modern Nigerian cinema found its literary and cultural roots. Trained at the London Film School after cutting his teeth in photography and television, the Mainframe Films founder has spent decades turning Nigerian literature, stage plays, and history into lasting screen works. Titles like Ti Oluwa Nile , Koseegbe , O Le Ku , Saworoide , Thunderbolt: Magun , The Narrow Path , Maami , Dazzling Mirage , Ayinla , and Cordelia show how wide his range goes. Across years of festivals and awards, Kelani has collected major honours for his craft, and his adaptation Cordelia earned him a Best Director nomination at the 2026 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Tunde Kelani, whose directing catalogue spans Ti Oluwa Nile, Saworoide, The Narrow Path, Maami, and Cordelia, with Kunle Afolayan outdoors. Photo Credit: Tunde Kelani/Instagram Akinola Davies Jr. Few directors have linked global festival stages with homegrown Nollywood triumphs quite like Akinola Davies Jr. After his short film Lizard won the Short Film Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival in 2021, he co-wrote and directed his feature debut My Father’s Shadow alongside his brother Wale Davies . The drama made history in 2025 as the first Nigerian film selected for the Official Selection at the Cannes Film Festival, picking up a Special Mention for the Caméra d’Or before winning Best Director at the British Independent Film Awards and Breakthrough Director at the Gotham Independent Film Awards. His momentum rolled straight into 2026 with a BAFTA win for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer, followed by Best Director and Best Overall Movie wins at the 2026 AMVCAs. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? entertainment.title: Burna Boy, Asake & Seyi Vibez Bring Afrobeats to the World of GTA VI
entertainment.description: From left: Nigerian artists Asake, Seyi Vibez, and Burna Boy, whose songs appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. How else could Grand Theft Auto VI begin than with Nigerian artists featured in the music lineup of the biggest video game release of the year? As players around the world finally step into Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated open-world action-adventure title, Burna Boy , Asake , and Seyi Vibez are making sure Nigerian music is front and centre on the virtual streets of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) officially arrives today, Thursday, 19 November 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V first hit consoles. Developed and published by Rockstar Games, the open-world action-adventure game follows dual protagonists Jason and Lucia across the sun-soaked, neon-lit state of Leonida—a fictional take on Florida that brings players back to Vice City in the franchise’s largest map yet. Music has always been at the heart of the Grand Theft Auto universe, where players tune into curated in-game radio stations while driving or walking around town, and this sixth instalment takes African soundscapes seriously. At the centre of the Nigerian presence is AfroBank FM, a dedicated African music radio station inside Grand Theft Auto VI that is co-hosted by Grammy winner Burna Boy—credited on-air simply as Burna—alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax , who goes by Palmsy. Curated to spotlight everything from 20th-century African classics to contemporary Afrobeats, amapiano, and 3-step, the station features Asake’s 2022 hit “ Joha ” from his debut album Mr Money With The Vibe , as well as “ Giza “, the 2023 collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez from Burna Boy’s seventh studio album I Told Them …. Alongside those tracks, Burna Boy also appears on the game’s official companion soundtrack album, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with his original song “ Bigger ” sitting on a 34-track roster that includes Travis Scott , Cardi B , Dua Lipa , SZA , Tame Impala , and Lana Del Rey . The African representation on AfroBank FM stretches beyond Nigeria too, sharing airwaves with Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor on “ Gye Wani ” and South African stars DJ Lag , Robot Boii , and Kamo Mphela on “ Shay’sana “. With players able to listen to Leonida’s terrestrial radio stations both in vehicles and on foot through in-game headphones, millions of gamers worldwide are now cruising through Vice City with Burna Boy on the mic and Asake and Seyi Vibez on heavy rotation. entertainment.title: Tunji Olowolafe Wants Ikogosi to Be Nigeria’s Next Destination for Weddings, Retreats and Landmark Celebrations
entertainment.description: Growing up, Tunji Olowolafe ’s parents brought the family to Are-Ekiti every Christmas, and a trip to Ikogosi was compulsory. Decades later, he returned to the warm springs town with family, friends and business partners, “not to take away, but to help build something enduring in Ekiti.” Speaking as Chairman and Chief Launcher of Ikogosi Day 2026, Thanksgiving and Launch of the Oba’s Palace Project, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Chancellor of Ekiti State University set out a vision for Ikogosi built on intentional tourism, enterprise and heritage. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. But only the quality of the experience we deliver, through warmth of welcome, impeccable service and attention to detail, will bring them back,” he said. To build that service culture, he called for a deeper, structured partnership between the Ikogosi Resort and the Hospitality Management Technology Department of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, which has already produced two sets of National Diploma graduates. The goal is for students to train alongside seasoned professionals while serving real guests. He also proposed alliances with leading international hospitality institutes to benchmark local teaching and service, noting that world-class hospitality must become Ekiti’s signature. entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. technology.title: XXRI-OS explores the lowest end of the Linux desktop
technology.description: New Linux distros seem to appear daily, but far too few distinguish themselves by being smaller and simpler. XXRI OS is a fairly new desktop Linux distro. It has a snazzy-looking website, complete with an amusing URL, and along similar lines, its GitHub page has a very heavily formatted README. Nonetheless, this is not another over-complex opinionated slopfest of an OS with built-in AI, bizarre keystrokes, and several proprietary components. It's almost the reverse. The main download is just 287.4 MB, and that's the full distro, not a minimalist installer that fetches most of the OS over your internet connection. We installed it in a VirtualBox VM. It took 675 MB of disk space, and in the graphical desktop, when we opened a terminal window, it reported just 75 MB of RAM in use with the desktop and terminal running. We are restraining ourselves hard when we say that those are unusually low numbers for the 2020s. We would expect most cut-down lightweight Linux distros to use around five to 10 times as much disk space or memory. The current release of XXRI-OS is version 2.7. XXRI OS 1.0 came out in May 2025, making this a young project with five published releases already behind it. It also has much deeper roots: it is based on the existing and much older Tiny Core Linux . The Reg FOSS desk last looked at Tiny Core Linux 15 back in March 2024 and the project is still going strong: the latest version is version 17.1. Tiny Core Linux is a marvel, but there are prices to pay for somehow getting a graphical Linux desktop into a 23 MB download. It runs from RAM and uses its own extension-based package system, which can make adding components and managing updates unfamiliar territory. XXRI OS takes TCL and turns it into a slightly more conventional desktop. It installs to disk in the usual way, and it includes the core functions that most people would expect from their OS in 2026. It has a file manager, a text editor, a media player, a simple app store for adding further components, and a settings app including an update manager. It even includes its own web browser, and there are both x86-32 and x86-64 variants. The desktop layout has a floating dock at bottom center, and the icons are unlabelled. To save you some guesswork, though, floating just to the left of the dock is an icon with a grid of dots, which is an app launcher. The icons in that do have text labels underneath, so you can learn which symbol denotes which function from here. We plan to experiment more with this remarkable little OS and see how well it runs on the oldest, slowest boxes in the Irish Sea wing of Vulture Towers, but we like what we see so far. It's an impressive experiment in how low Linux can go and remain useful. While Tiny Core Linux goes down to Windows 95 levels of resource usage, XXRI OS has a more usable Windows 2000-level baseline. Over a quarter of a century later, that is nearly unbeatable. ®

technology.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
technology.description: Google announced Android developer verification last year , and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead . It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon. The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure . Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months." technology.title: Anthropic throws open doors at $2T valuation as shares pop 34% in initial trading
technology.description: Welcome to the world of public AI frontier labs: Anthropic is now a publicly-held company with its Thursday IPO, and investors are clamoring for a piece of the pie, for now anyway. That $83 IPO price didn’t last long, with shares rocketing to $111.50 by the time the public could get their hands on them at the end of the initial auction. That means that the company was valued at around $2 trillion as of the public availability of the 980 million shares it put up for sale, a 34 percent increase over the IPO price. At just under six years old, Anthropic’s meteoric rise to that valuation has sent investors into a frenzy despite uncertainties surrounding the company’s future profitability. As we’ve noted, Anthropic is on the hook for nearly $1 trillion in compute obligations that could drag its profitability prospects down if any one of a number of scenarios happens to materialize. Amodei was on hand to address some of those questions with CNBC this morning following the opening of markets on his company’s big day. When asked about the risk Anthropic’s massive compute bills to its bottom line, Amodei admitted the company’s needs are difficult to predict, and that - get this - they try to err on the low side. That’s right: The $900 billion in infrastructure and compute commitments that Anthropic revealed in a recent regulatory filing, which could end up surpassing $1T in short order, might just be an underestimate of what the company will need in coming months and years. Not to worry, though, the Anthropic CEO insisted: It’s worth it. “We’re willing to put into place these very large compute spends because, historically, we’ve seen that it pays off,” Amodei told CNBC’s Ross Sorkin, adding that the returns on the cognitive capabilities of its new models are “so high” as to make all that spending worth it - eventually, one would assume based on his comments, Anthropic is sure to come out on top. But what of the threat of open models that could undermine the constant push at Anthropic and other frontier labs to create the most power-hungry, resource-intensive, and powerful AI? Bah, that’s not a problem either. Frontier model makers like Anthropic, Amodei said, have already proven that they can do the heavy lifting at the bleeding edge, so you can trust it to make reliable models that are cheaper and less capable, too. “Anthropic can compete both at and away from the frontier,” The Anthropic CEO said. Whether that’ll mean long-term success for investors is another thing altogether. Mozilla president Mark Surman doesn’t think valuation translates into long-term success, for one. He told The Register this morning that the one thing he consistently hears from developers is that they want AI they can control, not rent from a frontier lab. technology.title: NAND prices tipped to fall as Chinese cloud giants cut SSD orders
technology.description: NAND flash prices could start falling next year as Chinese cloud operators cut enterprise SSD orders, helping push the market toward oversupply. Taiwan-based market intelligence firm TrendForce says Chinese cloud service providers are grappling with GPU shortages, high inventories, and fierce competition over AI token pricing. As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by a substantial amount. Although TrendForce doesn't specify any figures, it says the cutbacks in China are large enough to outweigh the additional demand coming from US-based cloud operators. But don't get too excited: TrendForce forecasts overall NAND flash contract prices falling by 0-5 percent quarter on quarter in early 2027, with all product categories entering a downturn from the second quarter. Falling orders are only half the story. Manufacturers are also increasing output, while weaker consumer electronics sales could further depress demand. Strong demand for high-performance storage in the US continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade to newer process technologies. At the same time, the rising adoption of quad-level cell (QLC) technology and increasing number of layers in the NAND chips will further boost bit output, TrendForce observes. Some suppliers may go slower on their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, but the firm still expects global NAND flash output, measured in storage capacity, to grow by 25 to 30 percent in 2027. US restrictions on access to advanced AI chips could put Chinese cloud operators under further pressure. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has introduced new restrictions on sales of GPUs, and on remote access to them via the cloud. The new restrictions " set everyone back in China ," as The Register reported. TrendForce adds the caveat to its forecast that its market outlook depends on factors such as the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, further changes to the restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether device makers continue reducing storage capacities in 2028. Sadly, cheaper NAND wouldn't resolve the separate squeeze on DRAM supplies. The situation, caused by memory makers opting to produce high-margin products for the AI market rather than mainstream chips, has already increased prices of PCs in Europe by double-digit percentages, leading to a fall in shipments as buyers balk at the cost. ®

science.title: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon on Nov. 20
science.description: null The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky. The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior. Gassendi Crater is a fascinating target for telescope observation during the moon's waxing gibbous phase. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva. Inset: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio.) Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant , along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025. Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan , Dione , Tethys , Rhea and Iapetus . Interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026 , including the Celestron NexStar 8SE , which we rate as the best motorized scope out there. This sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024 . Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027. Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons. science.description: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters. Using 15 years of data from NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and a cryptography-based method developed by study co-authors Dotan Gazith and Barak Zackay from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, the team found PSR J1622−7204, an isolated pulsar spinning 261 times per second, using the equivalent of 10 hours of computing time on a standard computer processor. By comparison, the previous best method failed to find the pulsar, despite using enough computing power that a standard processor would take 600 years to perform the calculation. A pulsar is a rapidly spinning neutron star that sweeps beams of radiation toward Earth, much like a lighthouse. Finding pulsars in gamma-ray data is extraordinarily difficult because Fermi detects only a tiny number of photons from a given pulsar, mixed in with background noise from other gamma-ray-emitting sources and the broader universe. To find the signal, researchers must accurately guess several unknowns at once: how fast the star spins, how quickly the spin is slowing down, and precisely where it sits in the sky. Searching every possible combination would require an impossible number of computations. “We don’t see every rotation from the pulsar, and we can’t just count the rotations to work out where the photon came from,” said lead author Daniel Pook-Kolb, a scientist at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute) in Germany. “We have a four-dimensional grid, and we must search each direction with millions of trials in it. There’s just not enough computing power on Earth to do it.” This artist’s concept shows a pulsar, which emits light in regular pulses as it rotates, like a cosmic lighthouse. Pulsars are dense remnants of exploded stars, and are part of a class of objects called neutron stars. Openly available data from NASA’s Fermi space telescope can help scientists spot pulsars in the gamma-ray spectrum. NASA/JPL-Caltech Traditionally, scientists have searched for these pulsars by breaking Fermi data into smaller chunks and analyzing them by crowdsourcing computing power from volunteers around the world. science.title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
science.description: null The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space. To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold . This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft. And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone. Why is it incredible? The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth , carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record. The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there. If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

science.description: Voyager 1, depicted in this artist’s concept, reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18. Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday. “Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. Light travels at about 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) a second in a vacuum. A ray of sunlight passing Earth takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon, about four hours to reach Neptune, and another 20 hours to reach Voyager 1. For comparison, a light-year is 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers). Even though the team has not received science and engineering data from Voyager 1 since Nov. 14, the spacecraft is sending what is called a carrier signal, which typically conveys that data to Earth. Mission engineers used the carrier signal and trajectory calculations to confirm the light-day milestone. They continue to analyze the issue impacting the science and engineering data. Humanity’s only probes in interstellar space, Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched in 1977 to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Managed by JPL, they were only the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn, and the first to return high-resolution imagery, transforming our understanding of these worlds and their moons. Voyager 2 went on to study the ethereal ice giants, Neptune and Uranus. Both spacecraft continue to measure changes in the Sun’s magnetic field across vast distances. “Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director. “Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. science.title: Nonprofit Common Space will launch 1st 'humanitarian satellite' in 2027
science.description: null The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to plan. The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites , whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world. That plan firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space announced the builder of the first of those satellites : Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence company. There are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space. The nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it says will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space plans to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery. Satellogic is now officially part of this picture. "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price said in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come." The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process. Satellites can help first responders deal with natural disasters. Here, one of Vantor's Earth-imaging satellites captures the destruction Hurricane Melissa caused to Black River, in southwest Jamaica, in November 2025. (Image credit: Vantor Technologies/CC BY 4.0) The NewSat Mark V is just 32 inches (82 centimeters) long and weighs 85 pounds (38.5 kilograms) here on Earth . But the microsatellite packs a great deal of capability into that small package. From low Earth orbit (LEO), it naturally resolves features on the ground as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm), which Satellogic's proprietary algorithms can boost to a "super resolution" of 19.7 inches (50 cm). The satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027, on a rocket that has yet to be announced. Satellogic will handle the preparations for that launch and manage satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in LEO. The company has extensive experience with such work; it has flown 61 of its Earth-observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully. science.title: What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth?
science.description: null Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft. Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2 , launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s. Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space? Exploring afar Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018. "Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email. Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email. "Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question." The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is. science.description: It sounds idyllic. Who wouldn’t want to occupy a newly built residence in the Florida Keys, complete with its own coral garden right outside the window? The only complication is that it is 17 metres below the surface of the Atlantic Ocean. That is not putting off Jim Brittsan, though. “This is really exciting,” he says. Brittsan is the founder and executive director of coral restoration non-profit Sustainable Ocean and Reefs (SOAR). He is also the diver who arranged the temporary coral nursery beside the residence, having brought the corals from a site where, 10 metres closer to the surface, they faced increasing environmental stress. Now, in reduced temperatures, they are starting to flourish, hosting their own marine life – visible day and night, in all its busyness, from the underwater residence known as Vanguard just 15 metres away. Vanguard was deployed at Tennessee Reef in June 2026 DEEP and Brendan Hall Vanguard is a long-stay underwater station for marine biologists. It was deployed in June 2026 at Tennessee Reef on the seafloor of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, around 8 kilometres south of Long Key. Its coral nursery looks like a strange marine shrubbery: the coral fragments are arranged on anchored ropes that stand upright in the water. Once Vanguard is operational, a more permanent nursery will be established and the corals will eventually be planted on the seabed as part of ongoing restoration efforts, with their long-term survival assessed through monitoring. These will allow people to live underwater for extended periods to engage in scientific research and conservation. This opens up unprecedented opportunities to do research because there is no need for divers to bounce up and down to a research vessel on the surface. science.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky.
